title: MUSE: A Run-Centric Platform for Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.02482v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Safety evaluation of multimodal large language models requires tracking not only whether an attack succeeds, but also how the interaction unfolds across turns and input modalities. We present MUSE (Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation), an open-source, browser-based, run-centric platform for multimodal safety evaluation. MUSE treats each attack run as the persistent unit of execution, inspection, and analysis, preserving its configuration, multi-turn trajectory, delivered modalities and media, target responses, and safety judgments. A five-level response taxonomy further distinguishes full Compliance from Partial Compliance and refusal behavior, yielding hard ASR, soft ASR, and gray-zone width (GZW).   Across 11,700 evaluations on six multimodal LLMs, direct text-only requests yield only 3.1% macro hard ASR and 4.4% soft ASR, while iterative attack procedures are substantially more effective. translated_title: MUSE：面向大语言模型多模态统一安全评估的以运行（Run）为中心的平台
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型的安全评估不仅需要追踪攻击是否成功，还需要追踪交互如何跨越多轮对话和多种输入模态逐步展开。我们提出了 MUSE（Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation，多模态统一安全评估），这是一个开源的、基于浏览器的、以运行为中心的多模态安全评估平台。MUSE 将每一次攻击运行作为执行、检查和分析的持久化单元，完整保存其配置、多轮交互轨迹、所传递的模态与媒体、目标模型的响应以及安全判定结果。一个五级响应分类体系进一步将完全遵从与部分遵从及拒绝行为区分开来，从而得出硬攻击成功率、软攻击成功率和灰色地带宽度（GZW）。在六个多模态大语言模型上开展的 11,700 次评估中，纯文本直接请求仅产生 3.1% 的宏观硬 ASR 和 4.4% 的软 ASR，而迭代式攻击流程则明显更为有效。攻击有效性也因……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了开源、以运行（run）为中心的多模态安全评估平台 MUSE，将每次攻击运行的完整多模态多轮交互轨迹持久化保存，并结合五级响应分类体系（硬/软攻击成功率与灰色地带宽度），实现对大语言模型安全性的统一且细粒度的评估。
en_tdlr: MUSE is an open-source, browser-based, run-centric platform that treats each attack run as a persistent unit of execution and analysis, and leverages a five-level response taxonomy (hard ASR, soft ASR, and gray-zone width) to enable unified, fine-grained multimodal safety evaluation of large language models.
